key_insight: A two-local Ising formulation of linear-elastic homogenization yields one-local stress observables, allowing effective stress to be read from the same computational-basis measurements used for energy.
engineering_relevance: The formulation enables direct extraction of homogenized stress for multiscale mechanics without reconstructing the microscopic displacement field or adding a measurement basis.
method: Encode the reduced finite-element RVE energy as a QUBO and map it to an Ising Hamiltonian.
Approximate equilibrium ground states with a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE).
Differentiate the strain-dependent Hamiltonian using Hellmann–Feynman theory to obtain stress observables containing only identity and single-qubit Pauli-Z terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a demonstration on a two-dimensional periodic RVE but provides no quantitative accuracy, hardware performance, or scaling results.
watch_item: Finite encoding resolution and approximate VQE convergence can affect stress accuracy; the abstract does not establish a computational advantage.
paper_title: Ising-Encoded Computational Homogenization: Stress as a Quantum Observable
